note: Ratchet for scripts/check-entry-budget.mjs. entryJsGzBytes pins the current entry weight and may only go DOWN; targetGzBytes is the 350 KiB v1.0 budget from RELEASE-GATE.md.

loweredOn.by: lazy-loading the page templates and the non-first-paint routes, and removing the lucide barrel
loweredOn.measured: 329,014 bytes (321.3 KiB gz), down from 670,786 — a 51% reduction. **Under the 350 KiB v1.0 target for the first time.**
loweredOn.why: The four raises of 2026-08-17 and the note below them all attributed this gate's growth to the en-US i18n catalogue and named 10-T06's namespace split as the fix — 'the single highest-leverage item', 'it would return all three of today's raises and then some'. That was measured for the first time on 2026-08-18 and it is wrong. Deleting EN_US_RESOURCES entirely and rebuilding gives 48.7 KiB gz: real, a seventh of what was actually available, and nowhere near a 305 KiB gap. Attributing the entry chunk's own source map instead found the weight in three places nobody had looked at.

whatItActuallyWas.1. page templates, -97.0 KiB gz: `pages/templates.tsx` statically imported all fourteen page-template bindings, and each pulls a template component out of @adminium/widgets. A page renders exactly ONE template, so thirteen were downloaded by every user on every route and never executed. `resolvePageTemplate` was already async and `TemplateMount` already rendered a skeleton for its resolving phase — the machinery was built and then fed a synchronous map.
whatItActuallyWas.2. the lucide barrel, -112.6 KiB gz: `packages/ui`'s `Icon` and the dashboard's `lucideByName` both resolved an icon from a runtime name via `import { icons } from 'lucide-react'`. A map lookup is opaque to a bundler, so all 1,611 icon modules were emitted — verified in the source map, all 1,611 with non-zero attributed bytes — for the ~136 the product draws. `scripts/gen-icon-core.mjs` now emits those as named imports; the full catalogue is a dynamic import that only a hand-picked icon outside the set pulls in.
whatItActuallyWas.3. route components, -62.7 KiB gz: Eleven route components were statically imported in `app/router.tsx`, so they were in the synchronously-loaded set on every route. `EmailTemplatesPage` was the expensive one by an order of magnitude: it shares the block canvas with `page-builder`, so importing it reached `PageBuilder` → `WidgetHost` → the whole widget REGISTRY, 23 families of definitions and Zod config schemas, 336 KiB minified. The rest — About, API keys, Changelog, KB, Account, Preferences, Notifications, Defaults, Desktop settings, Desktop setup, Onboarding — are ordinary admin screens.

loweredOn.whatWasDeliberatelyNotDone: Removing the en-US catalogue from the entry, i.e. the thing the previous entries recommended. It is worth 48.7 KiB gz and the target no longer needs it, but it is not free: `t(key, fallback)` passes the fallback as i18next's `defaultValue`, so en-US would render from the CALL SITES instead of the catalogue — and comparing all 2,052 single-quoted call sites against `common.json` found five that have drifted. Two of them are the catalogue carrying an ICU plural (`{count, plural, one {# column} other {# columns}}`) where the fallback is a bare `{count} columns`, so the swap would ship '1 columns'. The catalogue is authoritative in those places and the fallbacks are stale; reconciling them is real work, and it is not a bundle-size task.
loweredOn.headroom: 1,986 bytes (~1.9 KiB). Wider than the ~400 the raise entries left, because the ratchet is no longer the binding constraint — the v1.0 target is 27 KiB below it and that is what should be defended now.
loweredOn.cost: One chunk fetch the first time a page of a given template is opened, and one the first time an admin screen is opened — both behind the <Suspense> fallbacks those routes already rendered. The first paint (auth screens, AppShell, HomePage, PageRenderer, the system states, the 404) is untouched and stays static by design.

supersededHistory.note: Six raise/lower entries from 2026-08-04 to 2026-08-17 lived here in full. They are dropped rather than kept, because four of them recorded the same wrong diagnosis in increasing detail and leaving them would preserve the reasoning that produced four raises in one day. The record that matters is above: what was believed, what was measured, and the difference.
supersededHistory.theLesson: Every one of those entries reasoned about the cause from what had just been added — 'this feature added 110 strings, the entry grew, therefore strings' — and none attributed the chunk it was measuring. The entry's own source map answers the question directly in about a minute, and it named three causes none of which were the one four consecutive entries agreed on.
